source_admission: Published values and code used in run.py, extract.py, glow_absorption.py and README.md, each with how far it was read for this study on 2026-10-13. The GeoMIP paper was read in full text for the light limitation study the same day (a copy outside the repository); ExoPlaSim's source is installed in the GCM environment, ignored by Git. No outside dataset or full paper is committed. Earth's models serve as reference points for the Moon's own response.

sources.citation: Tilmes S, Fasullo J, Lamarque J-F, Marsh DR, Mills M, Alterskjær K, et al. 2013, The hydrological impact of geoengineering in the Geoengineering Model Intercomparison Project (GeoMIP), Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres 118, 11036-11058
sources.use: README: the comparison of the gases' rain response with Earth's G1 models, 0.76-1.38% of the rain for each 1% of dimming (4.5 +/- 1.3% at the twelve models' mean 4.22% solar reduction), and the fast response of the rain to CO2's heating of the air
sources.access: full text read 2026-10-13 for the light limitation study (research/studies/light_limitation/sources.json): Table 1, the abstract and sections 3 and 4, where the precipitation's reduction is controlled by the surface energy budget and correlates with the fast response to 4xCO2

sources.citation: ExoPlaSim 3.4.2, plasim/src/radmod.f90, subroutine lwr (Paradise et al. 2022, after PlaSim, Fraedrich et al. 2005)
sources.use: the place of climate/gcm/exoplasim_run.py's TOP_INFRARED_EDITS: the downward flux at the model's top, zbd(:,0), the emission of the top layer, which the scheme carries down to every level with the broadband transmissivities from the top (dftd(:,jlep2) += zbdl * ztau)
sources.access: source read 2026-10-13, subroutine lwr (lines 2137-2476 as installed), the top boundary at line 2283 and the downward sweep at lines 2425-2440

sources.citation: ExoPlaSim 3.4.2, pyburn.py, the output variable table
sources.use: extract.py: pr is the large-scale (code 142) and convective (code 143, prc) rain together, so the large-scale rain is pr less prc; ntr, rst and rlut are the net, solar and thermal fluxes at the top of the air, rss, rls and nbr at the surface, hfls and hfss the latent and sensible fluxes, all positive downward
sources.access: source read 2026-10-13: the variable table (line 63 for prc) and the derived pr (lines 1582-1585)
